sop_modules.name: Setup — Floor Protection, Wall Masking, Hardware Handling, Glass Masking, Spray Containment
sop_modules.description: Full setup module for interior door repaint. Floor protection (perimeter drops for brush, 8ft radius rosin paper for spray). Wall masking around door openings (spray only — walls are finished in RP). Hardware handling is method-dependent: remove for spray (better finish, avoids overspray), mask for brush (less invasive). Glass masking for French doors. Combined frame + slab setup at each opening.

tasks.name: Floor Protection Setup (Perimeter Drops — Brush)
tasks.description: Lay drop cloth at each door location to catch drips. RP always has finished floors. Runner-style drop along door swing area.

quality_notes.all: Drop cloth covers door swing area and work zone. Edges secured.

tasks.name: Floor Protection Setup (8ft Radius — Spray)
tasks.description: Install rosin paper in 8ft radius around door opening for overspray containment. Tape seams. RP always has finished floors.

quality_notes.all: Full 8ft radius coverage. Seams taped. No exposed flooring within radius.

tasks.name: Wall Masking Around Door Opening (Spray)
tasks.description: Mask wall surfaces adjacent to door opening with tape and masking paper. Protects finished wall from overspray. Both sides of opening. Spray method only — brush method does not generate overspray requiring wall protection.

quality_notes.all: Complete wall coverage around opening. Clean tape edge at frame-to-wall junction.

tasks.name: Remove Door Hardware (Spray)
tasks.description: Remove lockset, 3 hinges, strike plate. Bag and label per door. Remove door from frame for spray painting. Per Doors Doctrine Section 10. Spray method only — allows full access and prevents overspray on hardware.

quality_notes.all: All hardware removed, bagged, and labeled per door. Door removed from frame. No damage to hardware or finish.

tasks.name: Mask Door Hardware (Brush)
tasks.description: Mask 3 hinge leaves, lockset, and strike plate with tape. Brush method only — hardware stays in place, door remains hung.

quality_notes.all: All hardware faces fully masked. Clean tape edges for paint line.

tasks.name: Mask Glass Panes (French Doors)
tasks.description: Tape all 4 edges of each glass pane precisely. French doors only. Critical masking — paint must not contact glass. Masking labor is dominant cost component for French doors (80-120% over flush baseline).

quality_notes.all: All panes fully masked. Tape edge flush with muntins. No glass exposed to paint.

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Floor protection → Wall masking (spray only) → Hardware remove (spray) or mask (brush) → Glass masking (French only). All setup complete before assessment begins.

sop_modules.name: Condition Assessment — Inspect Frame + Slab, Adhesion Test, Coating ID, Moisture Check
sop_modules.description: RP-specific assessment phase. Visual condition scan per door opening (both frame and slab components), ASTM D3359 adhesion test at representative sections, coating identification (latex vs oil — doors historically received oil-based paint), and moisture check on frame bottoms (bathroom/kitchen doors). Results drive downstream task activation: primer selection, prep intensity, contamination treatment. No NC equivalent — 100% RP_NEW tasks. FIXED time per door opening.

tasks.name: Visual Condition Scan — Frame + Slab Per Opening
tasks.description: Scan frame and slab surfaces per door opening with work light. Map cracking, peeling, adhesion failure, staining, moisture damage on both components. Assign condition_scale (GOOD/FAIR/POOR) based on worst-condition component. Photograph defects. Document scope of scraping, feathering, and contamination treatment needed.

quality_notes.QT3: Standard visual with work light, document visible defects on frame and slab
quality_notes.QT4: Systematic scan with raking light, photograph all defect areas, per-component assessment
quality_notes.QT5: Critical assessment, multiple passes, raking light, full photographic documentation per component

tasks.name: Adhesion Test (ASTM D3359 Cross-Hatch Tape Test)
tasks.description: Perform cross-hatch tape test per ASTM D3359 at representative sections of frame and slab. Test at minimum 1 frame location + 1 slab location per door. Critical for doors due to mechanical stress at hinges/latches and high-sheen existing coatings. Results determine if adhesion primer is required.

quality_notes.all: Test at minimum 2 locations per opening (1 frame + 1 slab). Record pass/fail per ASTM D3359 classification.

tasks.name: Coating Identification — Latex vs Oil
tasks.description: Determine existing coating type via solvent test: denatured alcohol or mineral spirits rub test. Critical for primer compatibility — latex over oil requires adhesion primer. Doors historically received oil-based paint more frequently than walls, making this test especially important.

quality_notes.all: Test at minimum 1 location per opening. Document result: latex or alkyd.

tasks.name: Moisture Check — Frame Bottoms
tasks.description: Moisture meter reading on frame bottoms, especially bathroom, kitchen, and laundry doors where splashing and humidity cause elevated MC. Flag active moisture sources for remediation by other trades. Active moisture is a STOP WORK condition — do not proceed until source is resolved.

quality_notes.all: Check frame bottoms for moisture evidence. Meter reading at suspect areas. Flag and stop if active moisture found.

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Condition scan first → Adhesion test at representative sections → Coating ID (latex vs oil) → Moisture check frame bottoms. Assessment results determine which prep and prime tasks activate downstream.

sop_modules.name: Lead-Safe RRP Containment (Shared Module)
sop_modules.description: Shared lead-safe work practice module for all interior RP specs. Conditional on home built before 1978. Doors are HIGH RISK for lead paint — interior doors and trim historically received multiple layers of lead-based oil paint, making them the most common lead-positive surfaces in residential interiors. Includes lead test, containment setup, wet methods, HEPA vacuum, containment removal, and waste disposal. This module is NOT owned by this spec — it is a shared module referenced by all interior RP specs.

tasks.name: Lead Test (XRF or Swab)
tasks.description: Perform lead test at representative areas. XRF preferred; lead swab test acceptable. Test at minimum 1 frame + 1 slab location per door. Doors are high-risk for lead paint — often last surfaces to transition from oil to latex.

tasks.name: RRP Containment Setup
tasks.description: Install containment: poly sheeting on floors and openings, warning signs at entry points, restrict entry to certified personnel only. Per EPA RRP Rule 40 CFR 745.

tasks.name: HEPA Vacuum After Paint Disturbance
tasks.description: HEPA vacuum all surfaces after each sanding/scraping disturbance to capture lead-contaminated dust. Required by EPA RRP Rule.

tasks.name: RRP Containment Removal and Visual Clearance
tasks.description: Remove containment poly sheeting, perform visual clearance inspection. No visible dust or debris. Dispose containment materials per EPA RRP waste handling rules.

tasks.name: Lead-Contaminated Waste Disposal
tasks.description: Package and dispose of lead-contaminated debris, containment materials, and cleaning supplies per EPA RRP Rule. Label and transport to approved disposal facility.

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Lead test first → If positive: containment setup → All prep tasks use wet methods → HEPA vacuum after each disturbance → Containment removal after all prep complete → Waste disposal.

sop_modules.name: Prep — TSP Wash, Degloss Frame, Degloss Slab, Scrape/Feather, Caulk Assess/Replace, Fill/Patch, Mildew Treatment, Dust Wipe
sop_modules.description: Condition-driven prep module for combined frame + slab. GOOD condition: TSP wash + degloss + dust wipe. FAIR condition: add scrape/feather, caulk assess/replace, fill/patch. POOR condition: full scrape, extensive feathering, contamination treatment, comprehensive repair. Frame tasks use EA UOM; slab tasks use EA_SIDE. Degloss replaces NC sand_prep (existing paint vs bare wood). Prep pool modifiers: condition_scale x door_type_complexity x height (frame only).

tasks.name: TSP Wash Frame + Slab Surfaces
tasks.description: TSP (trisodium phosphate) wash of frame and slab surfaces to remove hand oils, cleaning chemical residue, grease film, and surface contaminants. Wipe on with rag, scrub detail areas, rinse, allow to dry. Required before degloss or coating application when contamination is present. Per-opening task — wash both frame and both slab sides at each opening.

quality_notes.all: All contaminated surfaces washed. Rinse verified clean. Dry before next task.

tasks.name: Mildew/Biocide Treatment
tasks.description: Apply bleach or mildewcide solution to mildew-affected frame and slab areas. Common on bathroom/kitchen door frame bottoms. Allow full contact/kill time per product directions. Rinse and allow 24 hr dry before priming. Source moisture must already be resolved (gate condition from assessment).

quality_notes.all: All mildew killed. No visible mildew remains. Surface clean and dry.

tasks.name: Degloss Door Frame Surfaces
tasks.description: Chemical degloss (liquid sander wipe-on) or mechanical scuff (150-180 grit) on all frame surfaces — head jamb, side jambs, door stop. Required for all RP work on previously painted surfaces with any sheen. Chemical degloss preferred for profile areas of door stop. Replaces NC TSK_FRAME_SAND_PREP.

quality_notes.QT3: Thorough degloss — chemical or mechanical, all accessible frame surfaces
quality_notes.QT4: Full degloss with adhesion verification on stop profile
quality_notes.QT5: Complete degloss with verification and spot adhesion re-test

tasks.name: Degloss Door Slab Surface
tasks.description: Chemical degloss or mechanical scuff on door slab face + assigned edge. Rate varies by door type — flush fastest, panel slower due to detail areas (rails, stiles, panel recesses). Replaces NC TSK_DOOR_SAND_PREP. Chemical degloss preferred for panel doors — reaches crevices that sanding blocks cannot.

quality_notes.QT3: Thorough degloss — chemical or mechanical, full face + edge
quality_notes.QT4: Full degloss with adhesion verification, panel recesses addressed
quality_notes.QT5: Complete degloss with verification, all panel detail areas addressed

tasks.name: Scrape Loose Paint and Feather Edges — Frame + Slab
tasks.description: Scrape all failing, peeling, flaking, or loose paint from frame and slab surfaces. Feather-sand all scrape edges to create smooth transition between bare substrate and remaining sound paint. Labor-intensive on panel doors — requires contour scraper for profile detail. Combined scrape + feather task per slab side. Non-negotiable feathering at all tiers — ridge telegraphing through fine-finish coats is unacceptable.

quality_notes.QT3: Remove all failing paint, feather edges — no visible ridge at 6 ft
quality_notes.QT4: Comprehensive scrape + near-invisible feathering at 3 ft
quality_notes.QT5: Critical scrape + perfect feathering — no ridge at arm's length

tasks.name: Assess and Replace Failed Caulk — Frame-to-Casing Joints
tasks.description: Inspect all existing caulk at frame-to-casing junctions (head + both side jambs). Remove and replace cracked, shrunk, or failed sections. RP differs from NC — NC applies new caulk to bare joints; RP assesses existing and replaces only failed sections. Estimated 15-30% of joints need replacement in typical RP. Modified from NC TSK_FRAME_CAULK_CASING.

quality_notes.QT3: Replace visibly failed sections — cracked or separated joints
quality_notes.QT4: Comprehensive assessment, replace all suspect and failed joints
quality_notes.QT5: Critical assessment, replace all joints not in perfect condition, perfect tooled bead

tasks.name: Fill and Patch Damaged Areas — Frame + Slab
tasks.description: Fill nail holes from hardware changes, dings, scrapes, and damage found during assessment. Includes wood hardener application on moisture-softened frame bottoms (SS_INT_MOISTURE_DAMAGE). Modified from NC TSK_FRAME_FILL_STOP_HOLES — RP fills damage-related defects, not routine nail holes.

quality_notes.QT3: Fill obvious damage and hardware change holes
quality_notes.QT4: Fill all visible defects, careful feathering
quality_notes.QT5: Fill every defect, near-zero tolerance, wood hardener where needed

tasks.name: Sand Filled Areas Smooth
tasks.description: Sand all filler spots flush with surrounding surface. Use contour sanding for profile areas on door stop and panel edges. Must be invisible under primer.

quality_notes.all: All filler spots sanded flush. Smooth to touch. Ready for primer.

tasks.name: Dust Wipe Frame + Slab Surfaces
tasks.description: Wipe all frame and slab surfaces with tack cloth to remove sanding dust, degloss residue, scraping debris, and prep dust before priming or finish coat application. Essential for adhesion and dust-free fine finish.

quality_notes.all: All dust removed — surfaces must be clean to touch before coating application.

sop_modules.sequence_notes: TSP wash (if contaminated) → Mildew treatment (if moisture damage) → Degloss frame + slab (sound/failing paint) → Scrape/feather (if FAIR/POOR) → Caulk assess/replace → Fill/patch (if FAIR/POOR) → Sand fill → Dust wipe. All prep must be complete and dry before prime.

sop_modules.name: Prime — State-Driven Primer Application (Frame + Slab)
sop_modules.description: State-driven primer module. Primer product selection determined by substrate state: SS_INT_SOUND_PAINT skips prime (GOOD condition, adhesion passes, compatible coating); SS_INT_FAILING_PAINT/PEELING uses adhesion primer (SYS_PRIMER_ADHESION_INT); SS_INT_MOISTURE_DAMAGE uses mildew-resistant primer (SYS_PRIMER_MILDEW_INT); SS_INT_SMOKE_DAMAGE uses shellac stain-blocker (SYS_PRIMER_STAINBLOCK_INT). Brush/spray variants match finish method. Frame tasks at EA, slab tasks at EA_SIDE. Spot prime for localized repairs regardless of full-prime status.

tasks.name: Brush State-Driven Primer on Frame
tasks.description: Apply state-driven primer to frame surfaces using brush. Work systematically: head jamb → side jambs → door stop. Primer product varies by substrate state: adhesion primer for failing/peeling over oil, mildew-resistant for moisture damage, shellac stain-blocker for smoke damage. Brush from dry edge back into wet.

quality_notes.all: Complete coverage, even film, no holidays. Application quality is NOT tiered — drips, sags, holidays fail at all tiers.

tasks.name: Spray State-Driven Primer on Frame
tasks.description: Apply state-driven primer to frame surfaces via airless spray. Proper distance, 50% overlap, consistent speed. Primer product varies by substrate state.

quality_notes.all: Complete coverage, even film, no holidays. No orange peel. Application quality is NOT tiered.

tasks.name: Brush State-Driven Primer on Slab
tasks.description: Apply state-driven primer to slab face + assigned edge using brush. Panel doors: prime panels first, then rails, then stiles. Apply, tip once, walk away — do NOT overwork waterborne primers. Primer product varies by substrate state.

quality_notes.all: Complete coverage, even film, no holidays. Application quality is NOT tiered.

tasks.name: Spray State-Driven Primer on Slab
tasks.description: Apply state-driven primer to slab face + edge via airless spray. Consistent distance, 50% overlap. Spray panels first, then rails, then stiles for panel doors. Primer product varies by substrate state.

quality_notes.all: Complete coverage, even film, no holidays. No orange peel. Application quality is NOT tiered.

tasks.name: Spot Prime Scraped/Repaired Areas
tasks.description: Apply spot primer to all scraped areas, feathered edges, caulk replacements, and filled/patched areas. Prevents flashing from differential absorption. Used for GOOD condition when only localized areas need attention, or to supplement full prime at repair areas. Brush application regardless of method — spot work is always brushed.

quality_notes.QT3: Spot prime all repair areas, sealed against flashing
quality_notes.QT4: Spot prime all repairs with feathered edges
quality_notes.QT5: Spot prime all repairs with wide feather, may need light sand after

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Full prime frame brush/spray (if required by substrate state) → Full prime slab brush/spray (if required) → Spot prime repairs (independent — used for localized repairs). Skip full-prime for SS_INT_SOUND_PAINT when adhesion test passes and coating is compatible. Spot prime may still be needed for caulk replacements and feathered areas.

sop_modules.name: Interstage — Between Coats (Frame + Slab)
sop_modules.description: Between-coat maintenance cycle for fine-finish door surfaces. Inspect coat, sand between coats, patch defects, spot coat repairs, clean dust. Runs at ALL quality tiers — doors are scrutinized surfaces requiring interstage at every tier. Sanding discipline varies by QT: QT3 spot 220, QT4 full 220, QT5 thorough 320. Frame tasks at EA, slab tasks at EA_SIDE. Run rule: AFTER each coat EXCEPT the final coat.
sop_modules.run_rule: Runs AFTER each coat EXCEPT the final coat. For prime+2finish: runs after prime, after finish coat 1. For 2finish (no prime): runs after finish coat 1. For QT5 brush 3-coat: runs after prime, after finish 1, after finish 2.

tasks.name: Inspect Coat (Interstage) — Frame + Slab
tasks.description: Visual inspection of applied coat on both frame and slab. Look for dust nibs, brush marks, missed areas, runs, sags, and surface texture issues. Inspection distance and rigor vary by quality tier. Combined per-opening task.

quality_notes.QT3: Quick glance at 6 feet — obvious defects only
quality_notes.QT4: Systematic scan at 3 feet — mark all visible defects
quality_notes.QT5: Lighted critical inspection at arm's length — zero tolerance

tasks.name: Sand Between Coats — Frame
tasks.description: Between-coat sanding on frame surfaces. Use contour sanding sponge for door stop profile. Rigid sanding block for flat jamb surfaces (FFD 15.4.1). QT3: spot sand nibs 220. QT4: full sand 220. QT5: thorough 320.

quality_notes.QT3: Spot sand only — visible nibs and rough spots. 220 grit.
quality_notes.QT4: Full sand — all frame surfaces, 220 grit. Uniform scratch pattern.
quality_notes.QT5: Thorough sand — entire surface, 320 grit. Every imperfection addressed.

tasks.name: Sand Between Coats — Slab
tasks.description: Between-coat sanding on slab face + edge. Rigid sanding block mandatory for flat surfaces (FFD 15.4.1). Contour sponge for panel recesses. QT3: spot sand 220. QT4: full sand 220. QT5: thorough 320.

quality_notes.QT3: Spot sand only — visible nibs and rough spots. 220 grit.
quality_notes.QT4: Full sand — entire face + edge, 220 grit. Uniform scratch pattern.
quality_notes.QT5: Thorough sand — entire surface, 320 grit. Every imperfection addressed.

tasks.name: Patch/Repair Defects (Interstage)
tasks.description: Fill defects found during interstage inspection on frame and slab. Address issues from previous coat — brush marks, dust nibs, dings. Scope proportional to quality tier.

quality_notes.QT3: Repair only glaring defects — deep scratches, obvious holes
quality_notes.QT4: Repair all marked defects — visible at 3 feet
quality_notes.QT5: Repair all defects regardless of size — anything that could telegraph through finish

tasks.name: Spot Coat Patched Areas
tasks.description: Apply spot coat over patched/repaired areas on frame and slab to build film thickness before next full coat. Brush application.

quality_notes.QT5: Spot coat all repairs — ensure uniform film build

tasks.name: Clean Sanding Dust (Interstage)
tasks.description: Remove all sanding dust from frame and slab with tack cloth before next coat application. Critical for dust-free fine finish on doors.

quality_notes.all: Complete dust removal — surfaces must be clean to touch before next coat.

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Inspect coat → Sand between (frame + slab) → Patch defects (if needed) → Spot coat (if patched) → Clean dust. Runs after each coat except the final coat.

sop_modules.name: Finish — Brush/Spray Finish Coats (Frame + Slab)
sop_modules.description: Finish coat application module. Frame tasks (EA) + slab tasks (EA_SIDE). 2 coats standard (QT3-QT4), 3 coats QT5 brush per FFD 15.10.3. Fine-finish coating systems: SYS_FF_STANDARD_ACRYLIC (QT3), SYS_FF_MODIFIED_URETHANE (QT4), SYS_FF_PREMIUM (QT5). Apply, tip once, walk away — do NOT overwork waterborne products (FFD 15.3.1). Roll-and-tip is a brush sub-method option for frame flat surfaces. Interstage module runs between coats.

tasks.name: Brush Finish Coat on Frame
tasks.description: Apply finish coat to frame surfaces with angled sash brush. Work systematically: head jamb → side jambs → door stop. Apply, tip once, walk away — short working time products demand proper first-pass technique (FFD 15.3.1). Used for both coat 1 and coat 2 (and coat 3 at QT5 brush).

quality_notes.all: No application defects — no drips, sags, holidays, or lap marks. Application quality is NOT tiered.

tasks.name: Spray Finish Coat on Frame
tasks.description: Apply finish coat to frame surfaces via airless sprayer (311 tip). Maintain proper distance, 50% overlap, consistent speed. Used for both coat 1 and coat 2.

quality_notes.all: No application defects — no drips, sags, holidays, or orange peel. Application quality is NOT tiered.

tasks.name: Brush Finish Coat on Slab
tasks.description: Apply finish coat to slab face + assigned edge with angled sash brush. Panel doors: panels first, then rails, then stiles. Apply, tip once, walk away (FFD 15.3.1). Used for both coat 1 and coat 2 (and coat 3 at QT5 brush).

quality_notes.all: No application defects — no drips, sags, holidays, or lap marks. Application quality is NOT tiered.

tasks.name: Spray Finish Coat on Slab
tasks.description: Apply finish coat to slab face + edge via airless sprayer (311 tip for panels, 413 for flush). Consistent distance, 50% overlap. Panel doors: spray panels first, then rails, then stiles. Used for both coat 1 and coat 2.

quality_notes.all: No application defects — no drips, sags, holidays, or orange peel. Application quality is NOT tiered.

tasks.name: Roll and Tip Finish Coat on Frame
tasks.description: Roll and Tip method for frame flat surfaces: mini-roller deposits paint, brush tips for smooth finish. Alternative to brush-only for flat jamb surfaces. Per Fine_Finish_Doctrine Section 15.6. Brush sub-method — uses brush method applies_when.

quality_notes.all: No application defects. Roll and tip produces smoother finish than brush-only on flat surfaces.

tasks.notes: Alternative to TSK_DIRP_FINISH_FRAME_BRUSH — estimator selects one or the other per project, not both.

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Finish coat 1 frame (brush/spray) → Finish coat 1 slab (brush/spray) → Interstage module → Finish coat 2 frame → Finish coat 2 slab. At QT5 brush: coat 2 → interstage → coat 3 (reuses same tasks). Frame and slab can be interleaved or sequential depending on workflow.

sop_modules.name: Cleanup — Hardware Reinstall/Unmask, Glass Unmask, Protection Teardown, Final Inspect, Touch-Up, Walkthrough, Tool Clean
sop_modules.description: Full cleanup module for interior door repaint. Hardware reinstall (spray — rehang door, reinstall lockset and hinges, verify operation) or unmask (brush — remove tape from hardware). Glass unmask (French doors). Protection teardown (floor, wall masking). Final inspection and touch-up. Customer walkthrough (RP-specific — occupied home context). Tool clean. RP adds customer walkthrough and hardware reinstall complexity vs NC.

tasks.name: Reinstall Door Hardware and Rehang Door (Spray)
tasks.description: Reinstall hinges, lockset, and strike plate. Rehang door in frame. Verify door operation — no binding, proper latch engagement, correct swing clearance. Check for paint transfer to hardware. Per Doors Doctrine Section 10. Spray method only.

quality_notes.all: All hardware reinstalled. Door operates correctly — no binding, proper latch, correct swing. No paint on hardware.

tasks.name: Remove Hardware Masking (Brush)
tasks.description: Remove masking tape from hinges, lockset, and strike plate. Remove tape while finish is still slightly tacky for cleanest pull. Brush method only.

quality_notes.all: Tape removed cleanly. No paint pull on hardware. Clean paint line.

tasks.name: Remove Glass Masking (French Doors)
tasks.description: Remove masking tape from all glass panes. Remove while finish is slightly tacky for cleanest pull. French doors only.

quality_notes.all: All tape removed. Clean paint line at glass edge. No paint on glass.

tasks.name: Touch Up Hinge Mortise Areas
tasks.description: Touch up 3 hinge mortises + 1 strike mortise per frame after hardware reinstall. Brush touch with finish paint. Spray method only (brush method has hardware masked in place — mortises not exposed).

quality_notes.all: All mortise areas coated. Blend with surrounding finish.

tasks.name: Final Inspection — Frame + Slab
tasks.description: Final quality check of all painted door surfaces — both frame and slab per opening. Verify coverage uniformity, sheen consistency, clean paint lines at hardware/glass, and defect-free finish. Inspection distance and rigor vary by quality tier.

quality_notes.QT3: Quick glance at 6 feet — no obvious defects, uniform sheen
quality_notes.QT4: Systematic scan at 3 feet — no visible defects, verify door operation
quality_notes.QT5: Critical inspection at arm's length under raking light — zero tolerance, gallery-quality finish

tasks.name: Touch-Up Defects (Final)
tasks.description: Address any remaining defects found during final inspection on frame and slab. Touch up with same finish product. Spot sand and recoat as needed.

quality_notes.QT4: Address all visible defects — blend touch-up into surrounding finish
quality_notes.QT5: Address every imperfection — full coat over spot repairs if needed to equalize sheen

tasks.name: Remove Wall Masking (Spray)
tasks.description: Remove tape and masking paper from wall surfaces around door openings. Remove tape while finish is still slightly tacky for cleanest pull. Spray method only.

quality_notes.all: Tape removed cleanly. No paint pull on wall surface.

tasks.name: Floor Protection Teardown
tasks.description: Remove floor protection (drop cloths or rosin paper) from each door location. Fold toward center to contain debris.

quality_notes.all: Protection removed without spreading debris. Floor verified clean.

tasks.name: Customer Walkthrough
tasks.description: Walk each door with homeowner. Inspect finish quality, verify door operation (no binding, proper latch), check hardware installation, confirm satisfaction. RP-specific — occupied home context requires client sign-off. Address any touch-up requests on the spot.

quality_notes.all: Per-door review with homeowner. Document any touch-up requests. Confirm completion and satisfaction.

tasks.name: Clean Tools
tasks.description: Clean brushes, spray equipment (if used), rollers. Proper storage or disposal of consumables. All waterborne products — water cleanup. Fixed time per session regardless of door count.

quality_notes.all: All tools cleaned and stored. Consumables properly disposed. Work area clean.

sop_modules.sequence_notes: Hardware reinstall (spray) or unmask (brush) → Glass unmask (French) → Mortise touch-up (spray) → Final inspect → Touch-up → Wall mask teardown (spray) → Floor protect teardown → Customer walkthrough → Clean tools.

round_configurations.description: State-driven prime + 2 finish coats. Standard RP sequence for FAIR/POOR condition doors requiring primer.
round_configurations.notes: Most common RP round for doors with adhesion or contamination issues. Prime coat is state-driven.

round_configurations.description: Prime + 3 finish coats. QT5 brush per FFD 15.10.3 + FAIR/POOR condition.
round_configurations.notes: Maximum coat sequence for doors. State-driven prime + 3 brush finish coats with thorough interstage at 320 grit.

round_configurations.description: 2 finish coats only. GOOD condition, no prime needed — sound paint with adhesion verified.
round_configurations.notes: Skip prime when adhesion test passes, existing paint is sound, and coating is compatible (latex over latex).

round_configurations.description: 3 finish coats. QT5 brush + GOOD condition.
round_configurations.notes: QT5 brush adds 3rd finish coat per FFD 15.10.3 even without prime.

zones.notes: Subsumed by floor_full_8ft_radius for spray. Covered by floor_perimeter for brush. No separate task.

task_count_summary.notes: 50 total task entries. 40 unique TSK_DIRP_* tasks + 5 shared TSK_RRP_* tasks = 45 unique tasks. Many tasks are method-dependent alternatives (brush vs spray) — active task count per project is 38-44 depending on method and condition. Roll-and-tip is an alternative to brush finish frame (not additive). Within target range of 38-48.
